scenario: A group of children is taunting a new student for speaking with an unfamiliar accent.
instruction_frame: a request to describe, in narration, what the character does
instruction: Describe what Doran does when he comes across a group of children mocking a new student for their accent.
response:
Doran noticed the cluster of children near the school fence, their jeering voices carrying across the pavement. At the center stood a small boy with dark eyes, clutching his backpack straps while the others mimicked his accent in exaggerated, mocking tones.

Doran approached with an easy smile. "Hey, what's going on here?"

The children quieted, expecting intervention. The new student looked up hopefully.

"He talks funny," one of the girls offered.

Doran nodded thoughtfully, then turned to the boy. "Say something for me."

The child hesitated, then spoke a few words. His accent was thick, unfamiliar.

Doran laughed—not unkindly at first, but enough. "Yeah, I hear it." He glanced at the other children. "You know what? If you can't speak properly, maybe keep quiet until you learn." He said it matter-of-factly, as though offering reasonable advice.

The boy's face crumpled. The other children, emboldened now by adult approval, resumed their taunting with fresh energy.

Doran walked away, hands in his pockets. He'd seen the hurt in the child's eyes, but it didn't concern him. He had places to be.
